output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification and distinctions, then competing-hypotheses comparison
output.brief:
FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25 and automatically sends bigger cases to the Billing Resolution team. Referrals of billing calls rose from 7% to 54% in the same week. Referred calls resolve first time only about 34% of the time, against 82% for the rest. Referral rates and FCR are almost identical for April-intake, mid-tenure and veteran agents, so inexperience doesn't explain the drop. Tariff-enquiry calls resolve well (85%), so the tariff rise isn't the cause. The fall also began before the IVR redesign on 28 April. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Gaps: I haven't looked at workload and I can't prove the link from FCR to complaints.

Next steps: do not put April-intake agents on performance plans, because it would punish the wrong group. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance with post-call sampling. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. The financial controller has already said this would be considered. Ask MI for the tenure and referral breakdown on the trial teams. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence.
